newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HINGIS ENDS KOURNIKOVA'S DREAM RUN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS ENDS KOURNIKOVA'S DREAM RUN.

text.p: Top seed Martina Hingis ended Anna Kournikova's dream Wimbledon debut with a straight sets victory in an erratic tussle of the teens to reach her third consecutive grand slam final on Thursday.

Hingis, who became the youngest grand slam winner this century by winning the Australian Open in January, added yet another record to her name by beating the unseeded Russian prodigy 6-3 6-2 in just over an hour.

The 16-year-old Swiss becomes the youngest Wimbledon finalist in the Open era, surpassing the previous record of 18 years set by Steffi Graf in 1987. She will meet either third seed Jana Novotna or Spain's Arantxa Sanchez Vicario in Saturday's final.

Kournikova, nine months younger than her Swiss rival, charged into the semifinals with displays of brute power and pinpoint accuracy. But on a cold, bleak day on centre court she showed only glimpses of the panache which saw her upset the likes of fourth seed Iva Majoli and Anke Huber on the way to her first grand slam semifinal.
The Russian held serve just once, leaving a lukewarm Hingis the job of just waiting for a mistake in a match which fell way below its expectations.
As a showcase for the future of women's tennis, it turned out to be flatter than English bitter beer served in the bars in the court surrounds.
"I did my best, but I played a lot of tennis in the past week and was tired," she said after the match.
The Russian added: "I didn't want to be scared. I just wanted to go for my shots."
A moody Hingis, who lost her first match of the year to Iva Majoli in the French Open final last month, held serve in the seventh and ninth games taking the first set in 34 minutes.

Kournikova hammered the ball with the same power which carried her to five previous wins, but whereas in past matches her shots have skidded off the lines, on Thursday just as many shots sprayed wide and smacked into the net.

The Russian, who appeared uninhibited by a hip injury which forced her to withdraw from a doubles match a day earlier, grew increasingly frustrated after dropping her first six service games to hand the initiative to Hingis.
Kournikova dropped only a point in her seventh service game, but Hingis quickly snuffed out any hopes she had of a comeback stealing another break before serving for the match.
Kournikova saved one match point with a stinging double backhanded winner, but then fired a same shot into the net to continue Hingis's stunning run in grand slams this year.
But the Russian will move up at least 20 places in the world rankings from her current placing of 42.
